warning: Experimental. Retrospective comparison with recorded crowd prices on resolved markets. Not a forecast, trading signal or financial advice. Cofinance never trades.
question: Can a Python-only probability from price, volatility and horizon match or beat the Polymarket crowd on daily Bitcoin threshold markets, and does it add anything on top of the crowd?

source.disclosure: The v1 crowd comparison already reported the crowd, the untuned 720 h model and their average on both halves. No fitted candidate here was scored on the second half before this run.

markets: contested at the snapshot: crowd or the v1 model between 0.05 and 0.95; same filters as v1

candidates.v1: driftless lognormal, vol = stdev of the previous 720 hourly log returns (no fit)
candidates.ewma: driftless lognormal, EWMA hourly variance; half-life chosen from [24, 72, 168, 336] hours
candidates.student_t: unit-variance Student-t on the v1 z-score; df chosen from [3, 4, 6, 10]
candidates.crowd_plus: feature test, not a baseline: sigmoid(a + b logit(crowd) + c logit(v1))

fit: grid by Brier, logistic by maximum likelihood (ridge 0.0001); probabilities clipped to [0.001, 0.999]
selection: first half only: leave-one-month-out Brier; the lowest of v1, ewma, student_t and recal is the baseline (ties to the earlier name); then it and crowd_plus are fit on the whole first half
metrics: Brier (primary), log loss, ranking AUC; differences with a 95% bootstrap interval resampling whole days (2000 draws, seed 20261119)

claims.baseline_beats_v1: second half, primary horizon: Brier(baseline) - Brier(v1) interval entirely below 0
claims.baseline_beats_crowd: second half, primary horizon: Brier(baseline) - Brier(crowd) interval entirely below 0
claims.model_adds_to_crowd: second half, primary horizon: Brier(crowd_plus) - Brier(crowd) interval entirely below 0

secondary: the 6 h horizon is reported with the same procedure; no claim
one_look: the second half is scored once; results.json blocks a rerun
scope: Bitcoin daily thresholds only. Python only: no model output, no news.
